svg.title: CO₂ phase diagram with Venus's simulated cooling path
svg.desc: Pressure on a log scale against temperature. The path starts at Venus today, 737 K, 90 bar of CO₂, crosses the critical point, follows the vapour curve to the triple point and the frost curve to 195 K, 1 bar, then drops to 74 Pa as Frost Towers cold-trap the rest.
svg.text: Temperature (the axis is broken between 360 K and 700 K)
CO₂ pressure (log scale; each gridline is ten times the last)

path.title: Sublimation curve: solid CO₂ in equilibrium with its vapour
Vapour curve: liquid CO₂ in equilibrium with its vapour
Melting curve: solid and liquid CO₂ in equilibrium

rect.title: Sealed dry ice at 180 K: 2.4 bar of air on top, 280 bar at the base of 2 km

circle.title: The base would melt at 222 K

path.title: The air's CO₂ partial pressure against its temperature, week by week

circle.title: Venus today: 737 K, 90 bar of CO₂

g.text: at the triple point, 216.6 K, 5.2 bar

circle.title: All the CO₂ is down: 195 K, 1 bar

g.text: All the CO₂ is down, 23 August 2036

circle.title: Frost Tower cold trap: 133 K, 74 Pa

g.text: Frost Towers trap CO₂ at 133 K
the frost pressure there, 74 Pa, is all the CO₂ the air keeps

circle.title: Earth-like, 30 September 2036: 288 K, 74 Pa of CO₂
